approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of molecular graphs that have real accepted scores. Greedy score and arrival-order survival immediately admits useful offspring; score-band draws then choose first parents and distinct crossover partners from those current survivors. Connected-fragment crossover, optional finishing and ordinary graph-edit walks make a complete fresh surplus pool. Stable canonical admission rejects duplicates. A Gaussian process learns from the full chronological accepted archive using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity, and correlated posterior draws allocate the next evaluations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Every real accepted label immediately updates both ordinary survivors and the predictor archive.
approach.novelty: Test the aggregate contribution of adaptive breeder support and rank allocation by replacing their shared consumer with uniform draws from one immutable copy of the retained initial population. Generated offspring can still improve live survivors and train the predictor, but cannot become starting breeding sources. Earlier siblings fixed initial sources while retaining ranked draws, made current live draws uniform while retaining recursion, or delayed newly accepted sources by one feedback cohort. This control removes dynamic source membership and rank allocation together at one boundary. It measures that scoped aggregate; graph primitives, initial score-dependent retention and learned evaluation allocation remain, so the complete foundation contribution stays unresolved.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved behavior is the joint scored-adaptive breeder consumer in n-62daf219c70a: accepted offspring immediately change its source support and rank probabilities, while the available controls isolate different boundaries rather than this aggregate. The actual three summary.json/run.log pairs are successful and complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747 and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. The published actual-history audit reports 105073 generated-source draws out of 110295 draws, 2401 distinct reused offspring, 629 strict best-parent beats and 258 incumbent improvements; these are opportunity evidence, not identified mediators or required Child counts. Ranked initial-only control n-4d4b5eafa8b3 loses 0.260205546950089 and all fifteen endpoints. Indexed live-uniform control n-a56491c332aa loses 0.04599801243765703 with thirteen losses and two gains, despite more local parent beats and better selected-stream predictive statistics. One-cohort timing control n-4a649366619a loses 0.052369572312959654 with ten losses and five gains. Full-pool predictive allocation removal n-01b48dd09404 loses 0.12438789088524467; its learned channel remains active here. Frozen source n-ae12ccae8c7b is specifically a GP midrank-target experiment (loss 0.021067064526871015), not the live-uniform breeder control, and its raw-feedback versus learner distinction is preserved. None estimates the current fixed-uniform aggregate or licenses a whole-foundation claim.
hypothesis: Remove ongoing scored-adaptive source support and rank allocation jointly at the breeder consumer by using uniform eligible first-parent and distinct-identity partner draws from one immutable serial-ordered snapshot of the original retained usable initial LIVE population, including that snapshot in the inherited crossover-availability guard, while ordinary current greedy survivors and full accepted-label count-GP learning remain immediate.

finding_summary.headline: Adaptive breeder feedback remains valuable: fixed uniform initial sources lose 0.24468 in mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights: The experiment supports positive conditional value of adaptive source membership and score-ranked allocation together at the breeder boundary, even when every generated score still trains the predictor. It rules out a broken or starved learning archive as the explanation for this panel’s loss, and shows why parent-beat counts and easier selected-stream prediction can mislead when source quality and reward range fall. Chemistry agrees with this pattern: small fragments and acyclic emissions became more frequent, and compact free-amine/aromatic combinations were recovered inconsistently, despite many new cores and continued access to rich ring systems. Fewer questionable reactive bonds did not rescue the endpoints. These are observed chemical associations, not a demonstrated mediator. The earlier fixed ranked-source and live-uniform controls are compatible with this result but share its Parent; their losses cannot be added or used to infer an interaction. The experiment does not divide the value between membership, weights, survivor selection or subsequent learned allocation, and it does not remove retained graph primitives or initial score-dependent retention. The whole graph-foundation contribution gap therefore remains open.
finding_summary.results: Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59567 to 0.35099 across the five tasks and three matched seeds, a loss of 0.24468 against the registered 0.002 scale. Fourteen of fifteen endpoints fell; zaleplon’s third seed improved by 0.00046. Every breeding draw used an unchanged initial molecule, and 1,309 generated molecules that naturally had positive original breeding support were blocked. All 4,200 nonterminal generated labels still entered later GP fits; the final 150 labels had no later suggestion. Local best-parent beats rose from 629 to 2,033, while incumbent gains fell from 258 to 79: beating weaker fixed sources did not sustain improvement. Prospective selected-stream pair ordering rose from 71.1% to 76.1%, and prediction MSE fell from 0.01272 to 0.00197, yet endpoint quality deteriorated. Seed macro dispersion widened from 0.02659 to 0.07699.

molecular.headline: Aromatic starting-scaffold families persist, with more tiny fragments and inconsistent recovery of compact amine-rich or reorganized heterocycles
molecular.overall_character: Assessed n-c8e2f3c42535 against accepted code Parent n-62daf219c70a. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read: each has 300 accepted observations, ten initial and 290 optimizer emissions. No task is omitted and no smoke record is included. The evidence-index published template and original Parent policy node were used; historical gaps retain origin n-c55c3d520a2c as reproduced by n-62daf219c70a. All 30 files have the same ordered ten initial molecular identities. Thus cross-seed recurrence and shared initial chemical families are dependent evidence; structural resemblance is not an ancestry join. All 4350 Child and 4350 Parent optimizer SMILES parse and sanitize with the installed RDKit, which establishes graph representability, not route feasibility, stability, binding, toxicity or clinical usefulness. No new labels were obtained. The Child produces indole arylamides, diaryl pyrazoline thiocarboxamide derivatives, quinoline-linked phenoxy systems, aryl pyrrolopyrimidinediones, polyaryl oxo O/N heterocycles and large acid/amide/sulfonamide hybrids. Both saturated and aromatic rings are abundant. Child median heavy-atom counts in task order are 25/31/39/32/22; Parent medians are 25/33/31/30/27. Child has 341 emissions of at most five heavy atoms and 542 acyclic emissions versus Parent 123 and 129, respectively. These are emission counts with repeated molecular identities across seeds, not independent discoveries. Child displays 128 emissions with a covalent N/O/S–halogen bond and 81 with O–O bonds versus Parent 1329 and 273 under explicit substructure definitions; lower reactive-bond incidence does not explain or negate the endpoint changes. Conventional amides, ethers, phenols and amines coexist with O-halogen fragments, thiocarbonyl/hydrazine combinations, crowded fused/bridged topologies and very large aromatic conjugates. Medicinally recognizable chemistry supports moderate drug-likeness, but the mixture makes synthetic plausibility questionable. Child raw unique typed/generic Murcko core counts by task are 266/143, 445/346, 554/488, 388/272 and 343/235, with every acyclic structure assigned one shared <acyclic> core. Parent counts are 295/124, 404/277, 391/259, 584/406 and 208/93. These raw counts are not productive novelty, endpoint gain or chemically credible independent scaffold coverage. Leaders often resemble the initial scaffold families, and two central-task seed leaders are exactly the same molecular identity. No genealogy, new-core mediation or separate source-support/rank contribution is inferred. Digest stereocentre and formal-charge string incidences are zero throughout; RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral stereocentres in 1841 Child emissions but no specified atom chirality. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of protonatable amines. Parent leaders can be higher-scoring while chemically more doubtful. Reported score associations therefore do not justify imitating reactive halogen bonds or cyclic cumulenes, identify an objective optimum, or clear the unresolved whole-foundation contribution gap.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer emissions, RDKit heavy-atom range 1–50, median 25; median perceived rings 3, aromatic rings 2. Digest ring/aromatic SMILES incidences are 0.8908/0.8609; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. The seed leaders have 25/23/23 heavy atoms and three rings: a carboxymethyl-substituted diaryl pyrazoline thiocarboxamide (seed0, evaluation77, 0.3818586193406609), a dimethyl/methoxy indole fluorophenylamide (seed1, evaluation281, 0.38277504802042894), and an acetanilide connected through phenoxy-methylene to methylquinoline (seed2, evaluation171, 0.4394278959350887). These contain recognizable acid, phenol, thiocarbonyl, amide and ether chemistry and look more conventionally accessible than many Parent leaders, although the pyrazoline configuration is unspecified. Parent leaders score 0.39405142067435733/0.47411701813450596/0.438972502037081 and include N-halogen indoles, a cumulated side chain or adjacent carbonyls; the slight Child seed2 gain is a contrary cell to a uniformly poorer chemical outcome. The last seed0 emission is ethene at zero, while the last seed2 emission is a much larger acid/amide hybrid at 3.7230122863852066e-08; final emitted molecules are not endpoint incumbents.
liabilities: OBr, COF and C#SCl show chemically questionable heteroatom–halogen or sulfur bond environments; sanitize success does not imply stable isolable molecules.
Pyrazoline stereogenic centres remain unspecified, and thiocarbonyl/N–N combinations require chemical scrutiny.
missing_features: The emission stream does not consistently preserve the compact aromatic/polar arrangement shown by its own leaders; 95 emissions are acyclic and 69 have at most five heavy atoms.

No specific absent target heterocycle can be established from these trajectories; the leaders already have useful ring systems, and broader local arrangements remain underexplored relative to the represented initial families.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial best is a trimethoxy indole fluorophenylamide at 0.3051048083696145. Compact retained aromatic families with modified methyl/methoxy substitution, amide/ether connectors or carboxymethyl pyrazoline chemistry score above that starting molecule. C=C, C#SCl, OBr and several small halogenated rings score zero. Large recombined acid/amide structures can also score near zero. This is an association with an intermediate-sized, organized aromatic/polar arrangement, not a monotonic reward for more rings, more heteroatoms or halogenation; both the fluorinated indole and nonfluorinated quinoline leader score well.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer emissions, RDKit heavy-atom range 1–68, median 31; median perceived rings 4, aromatic rings 4. Digest ring/aromatic SMILES incidences are 0.9333/0.9149; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. Seed0's leader (evaluation99, 0.5908014212396369) is a 29-heavy-atom, four-aromatic-ring oxo O/N fused heterocycle linked through aryl groups to a cyanopyridine, with two methoxy groups. Seed1's leader (evaluation187, 0.5745098039215686) has 45 heavy atoms and six aromatic rings, combining an ester/phenol pyrrolopyrimidinedione and an aniline–phenoxy-methylquinoline arm. Seed2's leader (evaluation221, 0.5771564231073596) has 47 heavy atoms and seven aromatic rings, combining a cyanobiaryl oxo O-heterocycle with that same arm. These have conventional constituent groups but the latter two are large, heavily aromatic, synthetically demanding recombinations. Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935/0.6248206599713055/0.6178024026512013; their changed fused N-rich ring/linker arrangements include O–F, chloromethyl/fluoroalkyl, peroxide or unusual sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. Higher Parent scores do not certify those structures. Seed2's final indole arylamide scores 0.5401739643225711, below its incumbent.
liabilities: Six- and seven-aromatic-ring leaders have 45/47 heavy atoms and eight perceived rotatable bonds each; their size and connectivity complicate synthesis and may limit practical medicinal chemistry.
The worst large hybrid carries a tertiary alkyl bromide, and the stream also includes peroxide and heteroatom–halogen bonds; no reaction routes or stability assays were supplied.
missing_features: Alternative compact N-rich ring/linker arrangements are represented less successfully than the published Parent leaders; larger initial-family conjugates do not reproduce their scores.
Novel SMILES and 445 typed cores do not establish productive scaffold hopping: initial-family resemblance and chemically difficult leaders limit that conclusion.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.548381482770623. Retained decorated aromatic cores with additional ring nitrogens, nitrile or larger conjugated combinations rise modestly above it. Tiny fragments including C=C and CCO score exactly 0.5, so that plateau is not a sign of medicinal quality. The true observed minimum, 0.2828686387849938, is a large brominated acid-side-chain replacement in a sulfonamide-containing polyaryl hybrid. More size/rings alone is insufficient: the smaller seed0 aza/nitrile combination exceeds both much larger leaders. The stream supports sensitivity to the arrangement of decorated heteroaromatic scaffolds, but cannot identify a required absent pharmacophore or separate score terms.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer emissions, RDKit heavy-atom range 1–73, median 39; median perceived rings 4, aromatic rings 3. Digest ring/aromatic SMILES incidences are 0.8517/0.7805; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. Seed0's leader (evaluation171, 0.9040701977822159) has 34 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and a free tertiary aliphatic amine attached to a pyrrolidine whose ring nitrogen is arylsulfonylated; biphenyl and dichlorophenyl groups supply substantial hydrophobic surface. It has no carboxylic acid or amide carbonyl. Seed1's leader (evaluation268, 0.060512944327108235) has 38 heavy atoms and retains a carboxylic acid, polyaryl/methoxy/F substitution and a secondary amine leading to an N-sulfonylpyrrolidine. Seed2's leader (evaluation189, 0.08568551808430425) has 40 heavy atoms and acid, imino/amidine-like and N-sulfonylated saturated heterocycle features. Both have four rings and three aromatic rings: ring count alone fails to explain the difference. Parent leaders score 0.9999989177995104/0.9969753164881906/0.9999934235240012 and have 30/29/30 heavy atoms, accessible aliphatic amine centres, aryl groups and fewer retained acid/amide features. Some Parent leaders still carry extensive halogenation or unspecified stereocentres. liabilities: The seed0 leader has a tertiary amine and sulfonamide attached at one pyrrolidine carbon, an aminal-like local environment whose stability needs scrutiny; its high score is not a synthesis receipt.
Large polyaryl acid/sulfonamide hybrids, substantial halogenation and unspecified configurations complicate medicinal interpretation; a docking score alone does not establish biological activity.
missing_features: Consistent compact aryl/free-aliphatic-amine combinations across seeds are missing; one Child seed finds a high-scoring example while the other two retain larger acid-bearing combinations with low leaders.
Neither protonation state nor stereochemical identity is specified, although the leader structures contain potentially stereogenic saturated centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.01904115112334333. A free tertiary amine/polyaryl arrangement gives one large observed gain, while an arylsulfonylpyrrolidine carboxanilide at 5.8097637550351674e-05 and N-sulfonyl acetyl/alkyl-bromide examples score poorly. A sulfonylated ring nitrogen is not equivalent to an available basic amine. Conservative free-aliphatic-amine SMARTS matches occur in 177/870 Child versus 714/870 Parent emissions, and carbonyl matches in 653/870 versus 165/870. This is chemical association, not measured protonation, docking poses, or proof that changing either group causes the score. The stream lacks consistent recovery across seeds of the high-scoring compact amine/polyaryl arrangements; it does not lack nitrogen or rings generally.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer emissions, RDKit heavy-atom range 1–65, median 32; median perceived rings 4, aromatic rings 3. The observed cyclic structures parse, but raw core novelty cannot certify feasible bridge geometry or appropriate double-bond placement.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently recover the more reorganized amine/carbonyl ring arrangements seen among higher-scoring Parent molecules; a preserved quinoline/phenoxy scaffold dominates its leaders.
Explicit configurations of its spiro/fused saturated centres are absent, preventing a chemically resolved stereoisomer claim.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.1678386594791329. Changes that combine the retained quinoline/phenoxy arrangement with altered saturated nitrogen/carbonyl ring closure modestly increase scores. Tiny C=C, C#C, C, Cl and N#CN examples score zero. The Parent's leaders show that alternative ring connectivity at comparable size can associate with higher values; the Child's larger aromatic ring fraction is not sufficient. The two identical leaders are repeated discovery from the shared starting panel, not independent evidence for a new chemical family or for a necessary particular bridge.

Digest ring/aromatic SMILES incidences are 0.7391/0.654; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. Seed0's leader (evaluation291, 0.23826836459954653) is a 24-heavy-atom trimethoxy indole amide attached to a fluorinated, partially unsaturated five-membered N-ring. Seed1's leader (evaluation186, 0.24406129844184835) has 25 heavy atoms and an ethoxymethyl/phenol aryl substituent on a chlorinated N-methyl pyrrolopyrimidinedione, with three aromatic rings. Seed2's leader (evaluation86, 0.23206034417494048) has 23 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings, with diaryl substituents on a crowded N–N/O-containing thiocarbonyl bicyclic system. These are compact N-rich heterocycles but still initial-family derivatives. Parent leaders score 0.6510211907030741/0.4870057305679067/0.7208853668418119 and have 27/28/26 heavy atoms, more fluorinated imino/carbonyl N-heterocycle arrangements, sometimes N–F bonds, a small unsaturated ring or cyclic cumulated unsaturation. Those liabilities are retained in this comparison: their high scores do not endorse such chemistry. Child seed finals are 3.245714689283969e-05, 1.0758081433483446e-09 and 3.428399123436144e-17, far below their incumbents.
liabilities: Crowded N–N/O-containing bicyclic thiocarbonyl geometry and partly unsaturated small rings need geometric and stability assessment beyond RDKit sanitization.
There are 227 acyclic emissions and 114 emissions of at most five heavy atoms; huge oxygen-rich acetal/polyaryl hybrids and O-halogen fragments occupy the opposite unproductive extremes.
missing_features: Repeated access to compact reorganized imino/carbonyl N-heterocycles with conventional carbon-bound fluoroalkyl placement is limited compared with the higher-scoring Parent output; this is a coverage association, not an instruction to reproduce its N–F or cumulene liabilities.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent for the partially saturated and crowded bicyclic leaders; configuration-dependent reward was not tested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.0020944534688323298. Compact altered N-rich heterocycles improve substantially over those starting molecules, but the stream median is rounded to 0.0 in the digest. Large acetal/thioester/polyaryl recombinations give values as small as 2.165163271345225e-72; fluorinated indole derivatives or tiny fragments can also remain near zero. The higher Parent association is with a different imino/carbonyl/fluoroalkyl arrangement at comparable size, not generic fluorination, greater nitrogen count or simply shrinking a molecule. No unseen target feature or individual score-term explanation follows from this panel.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-c8e2f3c42535, conditioned on this immutable-initial uniform-source control with full accepted-label learning, Search seeds0/1/2 and 300 observations per panel. Across 4350 optimizer emissions, 341 have at most five heavy atoms and 542 are acyclic, compared with123 and129 from accepted Parent n-62daf219c70a on the same panel. C=C and OBr illustrate the tiny-fragment extreme; high-scoring emitted molecules instead show organized aromatic/heterocyclic groups. A nonzero small-fragment score plateau exists in one panel, so tiny size is not universally synonymous with low observed score. Conversely large initial-family conjugates can also be extremely low-scoring. All panels share the same ten initial identities. These are selected-stream associations, not full-pool screening or a proof of a particular breeder component's contribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful scaffold size and connected functional-group arrangements while exploring alternative chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal process needs ways to explore scaffold/linker alternatives while preserving coherent molecular size and functional relationships, using only its accepted feedback. Track productive accepted new typed/generic cores and incumbent gains with explicit acyclic convention and ancestry overlap; raw diversity or restriction of tiny fragments alone does not establish benefit. Retained graph primitives and shared ancestry leave whole-foundation contribution unresolved.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-c8e2f3c42535 under the same control and frozen three-seed observation profile. In one scored panel, conservative non-amide/non-sulfonamide/non-hydrazine free-aliphatic-amine SMARTS incidence is177/870 Child versus714/870 Parent. One Child seed reaches0.9040701977822159 with a tertiary amine/polyaryl structure, while the other two leaders score0.060512944327108235/0.08568551808430425 and retain larger acid-containing combinations. Those two leaders also contain potentially basic nitrogen: basic centres are not categorically absent. Other panels show high-scoring neutral heteroaromatics, so amines are not a universal requirement. Counts describe accepted emissions, not measured pKa, protonation or causation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably recover compact free-aliphatic-amine and aryl combinations across starting-panel seeds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent alternatives for carbonyl-bound, sulfonyl-bound and free aliphatic nitrogen environments together with scaffold/linker changes at comparable size, allowing observed feedback to decide where each helps. Preserve unfavorable and unchanged cells, and assess whether new combinations recur productively across seeds; do not hard-code a target pharmacophore or infer a separate source-support effect.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in accepted Parent n-62daf219c70a; re-observed with changed incidence in n-c8e2f3c42535 under the fixed-initial control, Search seeds0/1/2 and300 observations per panel. Current Child has128/4350 emissions with covalent N/O/S–halogen bonds and81/4350 with O–O bonds under explicit RDKit patterns; Parent has1329/4350 and273/4350. Current OBr, COF and CCOBr are direct examples. Conventional Child leaders can coexist with these liabilities, and several chemically doubtful Parent leaders score higher. The incidence reduction is neither causal mediation nor assurance of stable synthesis.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still permits questionable heteroatom–halogen and peroxide bond environments inside otherwise recognizable molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bond-environment-aware transformations should provide conventional local alternatives while preserving favorable scaffold and functional arrangements learned from accepted feedback. Retain the original gap's source and conditions; examine high-scoring reactive exceptions instead of treating sanitization or observed reward as a chemistry-validity certificate.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source n-c55c3d520a2c as reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; current n-c8e2f3c42535 still emits crowded N–N/O-containing thiocarbonyl bicyclic leaders and spiro/fused nitrogen-carbonyl structures on the supplied Search seeds and observation profile. Higher-scoring Parent output includes small unsaturated rings and cyclic cumulene patterns. All accepted graphs sanitize with RDKit, but neither trajectory scores nor perceived ring/core counts supply conformational or synthetic-route evidence. Current ring-text incidence remains0.7391–0.9621, so this is a geometry-quality gap, not absent ring capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not distinguish graph-valid cyclic topology from demonstrably credible ring geometry and unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring-changing proposals need credible alternatives sensitive to ring size, bridge connectivity and double-bond geometry while retaining learned functional arrangements. Assess productive chemically plausible alternatives with real accepted scores; raw core expansion and Parent's questionable score winners cannot establish a beneficial geometric mediator or whole-foundation contribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source n-c55c3d520a2c, retained in n-62daf219c70a and re-observed in n-c8e2f3c42535 on Search seeds0/1/2 at300 observations per panel. Digest stereocentre-string incidence is0.0 for every panel, and RDKit finds potential tetrahedral stereocentres in1841/4350 current optimizer emissions with zero specified atom chirality. Current pyrazoline, spiro/fused amine-carbonyl and crowded bicyclic structures illustrate the issue. These are potential-centre graph readings, not proof of stable configurations or of stereoselective score sensitivity; aromatic-only leaders can be achiral.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged molecular identities unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and graph transformations should preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity when chemically appropriate, while distinguishing achiral, symmetric or configurationally labile centres. Test stereochemical usefulness only through authorized accepted observations, with original source and conditions retained; this panel does not establish an endpoint benefit from stereochemistry.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
